gaps.sentence: It ___ no difference whether we leave today or tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Make no difference' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: The editors decided to ___ the chapter from the paperback edition.
gaps.explanation: "Omit" = leave out; the other -mit verbs mean let in, hand in, or send (money).

gaps.sentence: The company has ___ enormous losses this quarter.
gaps.explanation: 'Suffer losses' is the standard collocation for experiencing financial loss.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ sure that all the windows are locked.
gaps.explanation: make sure means to check that something is true or has been done.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: He was exhausted because he had ___ the cooking for twenty people.
gaps.explanation: do the cooking is the fixed phrase; after 'had' the past participle 'done' is needed.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: It took him months to ___ the habit of biting his nails.
gaps.explanation: break a habit (or kick a habit) means to stop doing something you do regularly.
